headline: REA Gives Agents Evidence for Reverse Engineering
lede: REA turns reverse engineering into a defined pipeline: connect an agent, select the artifact, run local analysis, and inspect conclusions alongside evidence and unknowns. Its MCP interface spans binaries, web apps, firmware, mobile packages, and desktop software without hiding the investigative trail.

headline: A Browser Globe Maps the Moving World
lede: God’s Eye View threads flight transponders, ship beacons, orbital data, and public cameras into a navigable 3D globe. The result is part visualization, part telemetry console, with each layer exposed for inspection rather than presented as unexplained spectacle.

headline: VoiceStudio Keeps the Production Pipeline Local
lede: VoiceStudio brings cloning, dubbing, speech synthesis, and audio processing onto the desktop, with models and project data remaining on the user’s machine. Its catalogue of speech engines and hardware acceleration makes a cloud-free workflow practical for creators handling sensitive material.

headline: Context Mode Makes Agents Read Less
lede: Context Mode moves bulky tool output out of the conversation and into sandboxed execution, returning only the findings an agent needs. SQLite-backed history, full-text search, diagnostics, and savings metrics give long-running coding sessions a rugged memory and control layer.

headline: Diagram Design Turns Prompts Into Polished SVG
lede: Diagram Design converts plain-language requests into standalone HTML and SVG diagrams, from architecture maps to timelines and sequence flows. Grid alignment, overlap checks, and brand-aware palettes give agent-generated visuals a deliberate, production-ready surface.

headline: Skills Builds a Shared Shelf for Coding Agents
lede: Vercel Labs’ command-line tool treats agent skills as portable, installable guidance rather than provider-specific configuration. Developers can discover, version, and distribute project or global skills across assistants, repositories, and CI environments.

headline: AirLLM Streams Giant Models Through Small GPUs
lede: AirLLM avoids loading an entire checkpoint into memory by streaming model layers from storage or host memory as inference proceeds. Quantization, CPU and Apple Silicon support, and selective expert loading extend the reach of large models while making the hardware trade-offs explicit.

headline: ArtCraft Gives Generative Scenes a Workbench
lede: ArtCraft places prompting inside a visual production environment where creators can block scenes, pose characters, arrange 3D assets, and refine a composition before generating. Its mix of canvas editing, world building, and model access favors repeatable direction over one-shot experimentation.

headline: xtool Takes Swift Builds Beyond Xcode
lede: xtool reconstructs essential iOS build and deployment workflows around Swift Package Manager and a Darwin Swift SDK. Its command-line surface handles signing, device management, SDKs, and installation across Linux, Windows, WSL, and macOS, making platform boundaries a tooling problem instead of a hard stop.
